ch20.anchor: the great fallen city of Shanghai
ch20.note: 'Fallen' throughout renders lunxian (沦陷): territory lost to and occupied by the Japanese. The 'fallen zone' or 'fallen areas' means simply Japanese-held China—no moral judgment on the place, but the plain fact of enemy occupation.

ch20.anchor: our Party, government, and military authorities
ch20.note: 'Our Party' always means the Kuomintang (国民党), the Nationalist Party that ruled the Republic of China and that Chen served—never the Communist Party, which the book calls 'the bandits.' 'Party, government, and army' is the standard triad of Nationalist authority.

ch20.anchor: the result plain the moment the pole is raised
ch20.note: The idiom li gan jian ying (立竿见影), 'stand the pole up and at once its shadow shows'—an effect that follows instantly and unmistakably from its cause.
